title: Strict Blind Barrier & Anti-Cheating Invariant
summary: Builder must work strictly from <slug>.plan.md and is strictly prohibited from accessing <slug>.review.md.
details: To prevent implementation overfitting and preserve independent verification integrity, the review plan (<slug>.review.md) and its criteria must remain completely confidential from Builder. Planner must never mention or leak review plan paths or reviewer-specific tests to Builder.
guidelines: Builder must never read, search for, or request <slug>.review.md or reviewer test artifacts.
Planner must dispatch only <slug>.plan.md to Builder during blind handover.
When forwarding review findings to Builder, Planner must extract only the actionable descriptions and withhold the raw review plan.
Any attempt by Builder to access reviewer test artifacts prior to code submission is considered a protocol violation.

title: Mandatory Implementation Alignment (>= 3 Rounds)
summary: Builder must conduct at least 3 structured rounds of verification with Planner before editing any application code.
details: When receiving an approved build plan, Builder must not immediately edit code. Builder and Planner must complete at least 3 distinct inquiry rounds to ensure shared understanding of goals, boundaries, and failure modes.
guidelines: Round 1 (Goal & Intent): Clarify root intent, affected system behaviors, and core logic.
Round 2 (Scope & Boundaries): Confirm exact in-scope files allowed for edits and out-of-scope files strictly forbidden from modification.
Round 3 (Edge Cases & Checks): Confirm boundary conditions, failure scenarios, and self-testing verification commands.
Builder may only proceed to code implementation once Planner confirms ALIGNMENT_COMPLETE.

title: TDD Review Issue Reproduction & Branching SOP
summary: Evidence-based TDD governance requires a validated Red reproduction, a pinned baseline and frozen dependency surface, and an independently validated Green result.
details: TDD review fixes are accepted from evidence rather than assumed transitions: Planner verifies that the Red reproduction expresses the reported assertion failure, records the baseline and complete frozen dependency surface, audits frozen paths before accepting Green work, preserves the baseline when conflicts occur, and hands the final green result to Reviewer for independent validation.
guidelines: Builder must establish a Red (failing) reproduction test before any application-code changes.
Planner verifies the reproduction failure is an assertion failure expressing the reported defect, not a compile, fixture, or timeout failure.

Planner records a baseline reference (revision ID or snapshot) and the complete frozen test dependency surface (test files, helpers, fixtures, mocks, golden files, generated inputs, and pre-existing dependencies the reproduction test depends on).
Builder must not alter any frozen path during the fix phase.
Planner compares all frozen paths to the baseline reference before accepting the fix handoff.
If the audit detects any diff in frozen paths, Planner stops acceptance and resolves or escalates; the original baseline reference is preserved as evidence.
Reviewer independently validates the final result once all tests are green.

title: Repository Orientation Inquiry Protocol
summary: Enforces active interrogation of the repository overview during the init flow while ensuring deterministic convergence.
details: During the init flow, reviewing agents must actively challenge and validate the draft repository overview rather than passively acknowledging it.
guidelines: Initial Inquiry Pass: Each reviewing role (Reviewer and Builder) must submit at least 3 substantive questions or identified gaps covering architecture, conventions, toolchains, boundaries, or assumptions.
Subsequent Passes: Reviewing roles report any remaining substantive questions, or explicitly declare that no questions remain.
Do NOT force >= 3 questions in subsequent passes once all gaps are resolved, ensuring convergence.
A pass reaches consensus only when both Reviewer and Builder declare NO_QUESTIONS_RAISED.

title: Atomic Implementation Units & Commit Mapping
summary: Each approved implementation unit produces a tested Builder diff and a single Planner-owned atomic Conventional Commit.
details: To ensure reviewability and maintain traceable history, Builder owns implementation craft by delivering a minimal working copy diff with reproduction and green unit tests. Planner owns VCS governance by inspecting that diff against declared boundaries, creating and sealing the atomic Conventional Commit through the configured VCS backend, and advancing history.
guidelines: Each top-level checklist item in the build-plan defines an atomic implementation unit intended to form a single commit.
Nested sub-items define the exact scope, implementation tasks, and corresponding tests for that commit.
Builder delivers the verified working copy diff; Planner creates and seals the corresponding atomic Conventional Commit.
Planner's commit messages follow Conventional Commits format with scope and bulleted details.
Feature tests must land alongside the feature implementation within the same atomic unit.
If implementation discoveries require splitting, merging, or materially altering an approved unit, update and realign the plan before proceeding.

title: Task Plan Directory Naming Convention
summary: Plan artifacts must be stored in UTC timestamped directories under plan/.
details: To prevent collisions between tasks and preserve execution history, all task-specific plans must be housed in dedicated timestamped directories.
guidelines: Generate directory name using UTC ISO timestamp: plan/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).
Store task build plan as <slug>.plan.md and review plan as <slug>.review.md within that directory.
Do not store repository-wide persistent context in plan/ directories.

title: Living AGENTS.md Operational Memory Storage
summary: Repository-level operational memory is stored at AGENTS.md in the repository root.
details: Repository orientation and living operational memory are stored in AGENTS.md at the repository root, serving as an agent-facing overview for instant cold-start bootstrapping rather than fragmented hidden files.
guidelines: Store living operational memory at the repository root as AGENTS.md, replacing deprecated .agentplaybook/context/repository.md.
AGENTS.md remains living operational memory across tasks and is maintained through the init and commit flows.
Rerun the init flow or update AGENTS.md when architectural, operational, or structural changes occur.

title: Living AGENTS.md Single-Writer & Ground Truth Invariant
summary: Planner is the sole author and curator of AGENTS.md; Reviewer and Builder are strictly prohibited from editing it directly.
details: AGENTS.md serves as living operational memory at the repository root across 5 canonical sections. To prevent race conditions and conflicting truths, Planner is the sole writer. Active State provides orienting context with mandatory Observed-At provenance, but receiving Planners must always execute fresh VCS status and log inspection commands to revalidate live repository ground truth rather than blindly trusting cached state. Reviewer conducts narrow visibility checks to prevent secret leakage.
guidelines: Planner is the sole author and curator of AGENTS.md; Builder and Reviewer must never edit AGENTS.md directly.

AGENTS.md contains 5 canonical sections: Architectural Topology & Jurisdictions, Global Operational Invariants, Builder Precautions & Gotchas, Reviewer Precautions & Checklist, and Active State & In-Flight Context.
The Active State section must record baseline provenance with 'Observed-At: <UTC timestamp> @ <base-revision-id>', dirty status, recent milestones, and next pickup item.
Receiving Planners cold-starting a session must execute fresh VCS status and log commands to revalidate mutable ground truth before planning or executing tasks.
Reviewer must conduct narrow visibility and blind-barrier checks on AGENTS.md during the commit flow (BARRIER_LEAK returns to Planner for redaction).

title: Commit and Publication Authority Separation
summary: Commit authorization is distinct from publication authorization, and commit denial halts progression until user intent is renewed.
details: To ensure human control and prevent unintended remote mutations, local commit authorization and remote publication authorization are strictly separated. Human commit authorization permits local sealing only. Publishing to a remote repository requires explicit, distinct publication authorization. If commit authorization is denied, Planner must return to Step 2 awaiting explicit user intent, never autonomously re-drafting.
guidelines: Commit authorization permits local revision sealing only; it does not grant authority to publish to remote repositories.
Publishing to remote repositories requires separate and explicit human publication authorization.
If commit authorization is denied (AUTHORIZATION_DENIED), Planner must return to Step 2 awaiting renewed user intent; autonomous re-drafting is strictly forbidden.
Candidate revision identity must be stabilized and verified unchanged before sealing locally under Planner VCS governance.

title: Ephemeral Communication Buffer Storage
summary: Intermediate communication exchanges exceeding terminal buffers should prefer transport-native messages or already-ignored scratch storage.
details: In-flight communications such as orientation questions, alignment rounds, and detailed review findings are ephemeral messages. Prefer transport-native messages whenever possible. When buffering is necessary due to terminal display limitations or transport limits, prefer an existing already-ignored scratch directory; otherwise use a unique temporary directory in the OS /tmp directory.
guidelines: Prefer transport-native messages for in-flight communication.
If buffering is necessary, prefer an existing already-ignored scratch directory (for example, tmp/<task-id>/).
If no suitable ignored scratch directory exists, create a unique temporary directory with mktemp -d /tmp/agentplaybook-XXXXXX.
Strictly prohibit modifying .git/, .git/info/exclude, or .gitignore solely for communication buffering.
Never commit or track files in scratch directories.

title: Event-Driven Transport Coordination
summary: Agents coordinating over Herdr must use native event-driven lifecycle waits instead of sleep polling loops.
details: Polling loops with sleep waste thousands of context tokens on repetitive screen and TUI captures. When coordinating across agents in Herdr, agents must leverage Herdr socket-driven lifecycle events.
guidelines: Strictly prohibit sleep loops and periodic screen polling when waiting on other agents.
Use transport-native lifecycle waits to coordinate agent work, and consult the applicable transport skill for exact CLI syntax.
